name: UT-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Kennedy running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger raised only ~$54k with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Kennedy's incumbency and roughly eighteen-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing a Republican win near 95% all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting competition.
model.watch: A late scandal or major independent spending against Kennedy would be the only plausible route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about seventeen points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Kennedy is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $970,000 with nearly $390,000 on hand. His Democratic opponent, Jonny Larsen, has raised about $54,000 and reported just over $1,100 in cash, leaving little capacity to compete. Minor independent and Libertarian candidates are on the ballot but show no meaningful fundraising or outside support.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Republican win at about 95 percent. The forecast is a Safe Republican hold, with a wide expected margin and low odds of an upset.
